sources.title: Control of the Burgers Equation by a Reduced-Order Approach Using Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
sources.journal: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
sources.relevance: POD reduced models for open- and closed-loop Burgers control; the present B1 is a modal numerical comparator, not a replication of that POD method.
sources.relation_paragraph_for_phase2: Kunisch and Volkwein used proper orthogonal decomposition for open- and closed-loop Burgers control~\cite{kunisch1999pod}. This motivates a reduced-model control reference; our B1 instead uses a fixed trigonometric Galerkin basis and does not reproduce their POD construction.
sources.claim_scope: Paraphrase of primary abstract plus actual benchmark source; no quantitative superiority or replication claim.

sources.authors: M. Hertneck, J. Koehler, S. Trimpe, and F. Allgoewer
sources.title: Learning an Approximate Model Predictive Controller with Guarantees
sources.relevance: Robust MPC and statistical validation of approximate control; the present empirical comparisons do not establish stability or safety guarantees.
sources.relation_paragraph_for_phase2: Hertneck et al. combined robust MPC design and statistical validation to obtain closed-loop guarantees for a learned approximation~\cite{hertneck2018mpc}. Our comparison measures control outcomes and request latency empirically and does not inherit their stability or constraint-satisfaction guarantees.
sources.claim_scope: Paraphrase of primary abstract plus actual benchmark source; no quantitative superiority or replication claim.

sources.title: Koopman operator-based model reduction for switched-system control of PDEs
sources.relevance: Finite-control switched-system reduction with Koopman models; relevant control precedent, not an executed baseline in this benchmark.
sources.relation_paragraph_for_phase2: Peitz and Klus used Koopman-based reduced models to formulate PDE control with finitely many constant inputs as a switching problem~\cite{peitz2019koopman}. Their work provides a control precedent for discrete input alternatives; our short-horizon candidate scoring uses a different predictor and does not implement a Koopman baseline.
sources.claim_scope: Paraphrase of primary abstract plus actual benchmark source; no quantitative superiority or replication claim.

sources.title: MLPerf Inference Benchmark
sources.relevance: Comparable inference scenarios and measurement rules; the present host-ready serialized endpoint is a specific software boundary and not a complete deployment service.
sources.relation_paragraph_for_phase2: MLPerf Inference specifies benchmarking rules to support comparisons across inference systems~\cite{reddi2020mlperf}. Our serialized replay instead defines a task-specific stored-observation-to-host-action timing boundary; its results are not MLPerf scores or measurements of a complete deployed sensing and control service.
